messages:
Nadia: Quick async on the autoscale modal UI I prototyped. Main asks: make min/max editing fast, make burst obvious but not bulky, SLO presets + guardrails, and small a11y/copy fixes. Prototype: https://intranet.redwood/protos/autoscale-compact-v2 :mag: Omar: Saw it. For min/max, can we support both a compact slider for rough tuning and a quick-number inline editor for precision? Like click the number to flip the slider into an input. Keeps the visual compactness in lists. Chen: I like a small slider paired with a number chip. But avoid two-way desync—if they type a number it should animate slider to that value and vice versa. Also support keyboard arrows on the number chip to nudge. Ravi: Burst placement idea: instead of a full row, show a labelled badge next to the selected GPU pool (e.g., "Pool-A • Burst ON"). Clicking badge opens a mini-popover with burst amount and policy. That keeps primary controls short and surfaces details on demand. Maya: Badge approach sounds clean. UX microcopy suggestion: badge hover text "Temporary burst: enables short-term extra capacity (billed at burst rate)". Use clearer text than just "Burst". Nadia: About SLO presets: add three quick chips: "Low-latency", "Balanced", "Cost-saving". When a preset is selected, show a small toast that explains which guardrails changed (e.g., max cap reduced, burst disabled). We should let users undo the preset with a single click. Omar: Guardrail visibility is key. Rather than hiding guardrails in an advanced section, surface a tiny icon next to the SLO slider when any guardrail is active. Tooltip lists active guardrails. Prefer contrasty icon so it's visible at small sizes. Chen: Accessibility: make the toast and guardrail notifications accessible via an aria-live region so screen readers announce changes when presets apply. Also ensure the pool badge state (Burst ON/OFF) is announced when toggled. Ravi: Cost preview: async lookup. Let's debounce to 400ms when sliders move, cancel inflight calls on new inputs, and show a subtle skeleton in the price chip. Use aria-live="polite" on the cost chip so screen readers get updates without being too noisy. Maya: Color & contrast note: disabled state for min/max currently uses 30% gray — not enough for AA. Increase contrast or use a pattern/line to indicate disabled, especially on small stepper buttons. Nadia: Keyboard flow proposal: pool dropdown -> burst badge (enter opens popover) -> min number / slider (left/right arrows) -> max -> SLO chips -> save. Include a skip link to jump from pool to SLO chips for power users. Omar: One tiny copy tweak: change save button to "Save autoscale config" when in modal, keeps purpose explicit in cluttered pages. Chen: I'll update the Figma with a compact slider+chip pattern, badge variant for burst, and add the SLO preset chips + undo toast. Will include states for keyboard focus and contrast checks. Ravi: I'll draft the aria-live/announcement behaviors and add a short snippet for devs: `// cost chip announce
$12.34 / hr
` Maya: Thanks. If Chen pushes the frames I can bundle the small copy/accessibility notes into the design PR. Ping me when ready and I'll assign the review. :rocket:
